page: Amazon Web Services r5ad.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7571 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled and dedicated CPU allocation. The processor operates at a clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled as a 300 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume, and network performance is rated at a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data reveals that the r5ad.2xlarge exhibits modest compute capabilities. In stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, performance falls into the bottom 10%. Similarly, Geekbench single-core scores are in the bottom 10%, while multi-core scores are in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show weak performance, with read-only large block bandwidth at 25.47 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 13.03 GB/sec. However, Passmark CPU and memory scores reach average levels, and Passmark CPU encryption tests also rank in the middle 50%.

The primary tradeoff of the r5ad.2xlarge is its lower raw compute and memory throughput relative to newer hardware generations, as evidenced by poor decompression and text processing benchmarks. However, the inclusion of 300 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage alongside a substantial 64 GB memory footprint offers a resource-dense configuration for memory-bound workloads. This makes the instance qualitatively cost-efficient for scenarios requiring large memory allocations and temporary local storage without demanding high-frequency CPU performance. It is suited for caching layers, database operations with moderate transaction rates, and memory-intensive data processing tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services r5ad.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring an AMD EPYC 7571 processor with 8 vCPUs, 4 physical cores, and a 2.2 GHz clock speed. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed by the Nitro hypervisor, it delivers 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory alongside a bundled 300 GB local NVMe SSD instance store. While CPU and memory bandwidth benchmarks generally fall into the lower percentiles, with stress-ng and Geekbench scores in the bottom 10% to 25%, the instance maintains average performance in Passmark CPU encryption and memory tests. With a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, the r5ad.2xlarge is designed for memory-intensive workloads that benefit from local scratch space, such as caching layers, distributed in-memory databases, and moderate data processing tasks where memory capacity is prioritized over raw compute speed.
